provenance.notes: Out family batch. Narrow, visual niche that is easy to own in one metro: buyers decide on fuel, clearances, seating and the evening look. No burner, insert or stone brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Wood, natural gas or propane: fuelling the fire
pageStructurePlus.contains: Wood-burning pits and fireplaces, running a natural gas line, buried or hidden propane tanks, ignition and remote options, and smoke versus convenience
pageStructurePlus.why: Fuel is the first decision and drives the price and the permit. Settling it early stops the quote from being redone.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Distance from the house, fences and trees, fire features under pergolas and covers, spark screens, local burn bans, HOA rules and gas permits
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers worry about safety and fines. A clearance page shows the builder knows the rules and keeps the job legal.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Built-in seat walls around a fire pit, circle sizes for four to twelve people, fireplace seating areas, lighting in the walls and paths to the house
pageStructurePlus.why: People are buying evenings with friends, not a pit. Layout examples sized by guest count help them picture it and spend accordingly.

pageStructurePlus.section: Masonry fireplace build from footing to first fire
pageStructurePlus.contains: The concrete footing, firebox and flue, block and stone veneer, hearth and cap, curing time, and the first small fires to season the masonry
pageStructurePlus.why: A masonry fireplace is a structure that takes weeks. Showing the steps justifies the ticket and sets the timeline.

pageStructurePlus.section: Seasonal fire feature care and burner service
pageStructurePlus.contains: Covers, cleaning burners and ports, winterising gas lines, chimney sweeping for wood fireplaces, re-pointing joints and a yearly service visit
pageStructurePlus.why: Fire features need yearly care. A care page turns every install into a return visit.

openers.line: People searching for a fire pit builder in {City} find {Business Name} with no site. They want to see a fire glowing in a finished backyard before they call a mason.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a fire pit buyer would find behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing goes to Facebook, where the stone fireplace with the raised hearth is buried under weather posts. A buyer wants every fire feature you've built in one place.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it goes to Facebook. Note the best fireplace or pit there.
openers.linkLine: Your fire features, all in one place: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site lists chimney repair and brick pointing but none of the outdoor fireplaces on your Instagram. The fire features are the work people search for and pay most for.
openers.hook: Compare the site with their grid. If fire features appear only on social, use this.
openers.linkLine: A site that leads with your outdoor fireplaces: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone your fire pit gallery loads dark and grainy, and the night shots lose all their glow. People browse fire features in the evening, on a phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone in a dim room and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your fire features, glowing on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask {Business Name} for a fire pit or fireplace quote except calling. Buyers want to send the patio size, wood or gas, and how many people they seat.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for a quote form. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A fire feature quote form with fuel, size and seating: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your night shots of a lit fire pit with the seat wall around it are the best sales tool a mason can have. They scroll away in a week.
openers.hook: Find two strong night shots of fire features. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your fire pits at night, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about a fireplace that's become where the family spends every autumn evening. That's what a buyer is really purchasing, and it's stuck on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about evenings, family or friends. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the fire features they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: The first cool September evening is when everyone in {City} decides they need a fire pit. A masonry crew that's easy to find that week books the autumn.
openers.hook: Use from late August to October, or early spring for summer builds. Name the season.

openers.line: People decide on a fire pit sitting around a friend's one at night. A quote form that works at eleven catches them before the idea cools.
openers.hook: Call after hours. A full or generic voicemail means the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A fire pit quote request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a stone mason. Skilled masons look at a company's finished fireplaces before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: A masonry company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You build fire features across the towns around {City}, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you work there. 'Outdoor fireplace' plus the town is the search.
openers.hook: Find towns in their posts or reviews; use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: A fire feature page for each town: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you build the fire pit now and the seat wall or patio next year, say so on the site. A full fireplace project is easier to start in phases.
openers.hook: Only if they mention phasing or financing. Otherwise skip.

openers.line: A gas fire feature means a gas line and a permit. Showing your insurance and the licensed gas fitter you work with answers the safety question first.
openers.hook: Check for insurance mentions and a licensed partner. Never quote numbers you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance, gas lines and clearances on one fire page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every fire pit you build hosts friends all season, and some of them want one too. They still look up the mason before calling.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or comments mentioning friends or neighbours. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next fire pit referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you finished is beautiful stonework, and the fire looks perfect in it. That should be the first thing a stranger sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest fire feature and name it: pit or fireplace, stone, fuel, town if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That fire feature, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is beautiful stonework, and the fire looks perfect in it.

I was looking for fire pit and outdoor fireplace builders in {City} and found {Business Name} on Instagram, but no site where someone can see your fire features and ask for a quote. I built a sample site to show the idea, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample fire feature site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a dark night gallery so fires glow, a quote form that asks fuel, size and seating, and a page on clearances and burn rules. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for masons and fire feature builders in {City}. I sent you a message about a sample site. Did you see it?"

IF NO:
"No problem. It's a sample site for {Business Name} with your fire pits and fireplaces at night, a quote form for fuel and seating, and a clearances page, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, then ask what share of their work is fire features versus other masonry
"It's {Build Range} depending on how many fire feature and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For your shop I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than one stone fire pit with a seat wall."
"Ten minutes this week to look at it?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before the first cool evenings."

objections.objection: Fire pits are a small part of my masonry work.
objections.handler: "They're the part people search for and fall in love with. A fire feature page brings in buyers who often add a patio or seat wall once you're there."

objections.objection: I get my work from landscapers and builders.
objections.handler: "Keep those. Homeowners who want a fireplace still search for one and pick from what they can see online. Right now that's not you."
"Good. Happy to hand over the night gallery and quote form layouts. If it's not live before autumn, the offer stands."

objections.objection: People see a kit at the big box store and expect that price.
objections.handler: "The build page shows the footing, firebox and stone that make yours last decades. That's what makes your price make sense."

objections.objection: It's summer; nobody's thinking about fires.
objections.handler: "That's why now. The site is built and found by the time the first cool evening sends everyone searching."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: a night gallery, a quote form, a clearances page and a few town pages."

bullets: Price the gallery by fire feature, with a night shot of each; this niche sells after dark.
A quote form that asks fuel, size and seating count is worth its own line; it shapes the whole price.
Peg the build to one stone fire pit with a seat wall, never to hours.
Include the clearances page in every build; it answers the safety and permit question that stalls buyers.
Charge more for masonry fireplace pages that show the build sequence; they take more pictures and captions.
Offer a gas-feature page only to builders who work with a licensed gas fitter.

Max with stage-by-stage pictures from footing to first fire and a timeline.
Max with layouts by guest count and lighting options.
Max when each page shows a local fire feature and the town's burn rules.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The yard where you buy firebrick, block and veneer sells to every mason around. Introduce me and I'll build their showroom and contractor pages."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply yards have budgets and a mason list that is your prospect list.

withoutAI.route: Licensed gas fitters on fire feature jobs
withoutAI.whoPays: The gas fitter or plumber, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The gas fitter who runs the line to your fire tables needs a site too. One word from you and it's built."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Gas fitters rarely market and depend on referrals from the mason.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every wood-burning fire pit you build needs firewood all winter. The local firewood dealer needs a delivery booking site."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A small business with a direct link to every wood fire feature owner.

withoutAI.whoPays: The lighting company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The lighting crew who lights your seat walls and paths at night needs a site full of your fire pits after dark."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Night features sell together; the referral runs both ways.

withoutAI.whoPays: The chimney sweep, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Outdoor wood fireplaces need sweeping too. The sweep you send them to needs a booking site, and they'll send masonry repairs back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Sweeps see every chimney problem; masons fix them.

withoutAI.route: Patio furniture and outdoor living stores
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every new fire pit needs chairs around it. The local patio store needs a site showing its furniture around real fire features."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same buyer, same month; the mason's projects make the store's site look real.

withAI.route: Firebrick and veneer estimator for the supply yard
withAI.pitchLine: "Masons enter the fire pit diameter or fireplace size and get firebrick, block, veneer and cap quantities priced from that yard."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties masons to one yard and cuts counter time.

withAI.pitchLine: "Fire pit owners text to order a cord and the assistant books the delivery, takes payment and notes where to stack it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small sellers lose orders to slow replies; the mason made the introduction.

withAI.route: Sweep scheduling helper for the chimney sweep
withAI.pitchLine: "Owners of outdoor fireplaces get a yearly sweep reminder and book a slot by text, with masonry issues flagged for the mason."
withAI.whyItWorks: Sweeps fill autumn faster; the mason gets repair leads.

withAI.route: Gas fitting request triage for the fitter
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners describe the fire table location and meter distance, and the assistant drafts a gas line scope for the fitter to price."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster gas quotes mean faster fire feature jobs for the mason.

withAI.route: Furniture-around-the-fire preview for the patio store
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers upload their fire pit area and see a clearly labelled preview of chairs and loungers arranged around it."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells full seating sets; the mason's fire pits are the demo material.

withAI.pitchLine: "Fire pit and fireplace requests get checked against the HOA's burn, clearance and height rules before the board sees them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards worry about fire risk and want complete requests.

softwareAI.name: Thank-you drafts for fire pit reviewers

softwareAI.name: Deposit and first-fire billing

softwareAI.name: Clearance checker on the quote form

softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past jobs with dates and their service price.

softwareAI.name: After-hours fire pit quote line

softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar and questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the pit diameter or fireplace dimensions and get firebrick, block, veneer, cap and mortar quantities for the order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their standard builds and waste factors.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with design approval and first-fire date
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers approve the stone and design, see the curing schedule and first-fire date, and download care instructions."

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to fire feature quote
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Stand where the fireplace will go, describe size, stone, fuel and seat walls, and it drafts the quote."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal add-on offer sequence

softwareAI.name: Fire feature project story writer

softwareAI.name: Commercial fire feature bid sheet

softwareAI.name: Smoke and wind complaint helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners describe smoke blowing back or a fire that won't draw, and the assistant suggests causes from your notes and books a fireplace check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their troubleshooting notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Mason apprentice interest chat
softwareAI.pitchLine: "People curious about learning stone and fireplace work answer a few questions about lifting, tools and start dates, and the promising ones get a trial day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs their requirements. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fire feature price guide for masons everywhere
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Masons everywhere field 'how much for a fire pit' with no easy answer. A guide built for one sells monthly to the rest."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for it; the question is universal.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer locator for a fire table and burner maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Buyers who love your fire tables and burners need a trained installer. A locator with night galleries of their work sends them there."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund dealer programs, and the fire pit client proves the installer side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members switch on a fire feature gallery, quote form and clearances page as part of membership."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Masons are under-built online and associations want to raise standards.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency licence for the firelight template
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies make fire features look dull on light templates. License the dark fire gallery and quote flow instead."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: A niche build agencies can't easily make themselves.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Shoppers buying outdoor fire tables and inserts at your showroom need installers. A network page of masons who build around them closes the sale."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Retailers lose sales when there's no one to install.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Restaurant and brewery patio fire features
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A patio with fire pits fills on cool evenings. A site that shows it off and takes reservations is the obvious next step after the build."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Commercial owners have budgets and the mason has the relationship.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A fire pit and seat wall package on the options page sells before closing and goes to one mason."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like option revenue and organised partners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents check burn rules and apply for recreational fire permits online, with clearance guidance and a list of local builders."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Fire departments field these questions constantly and want fewer violations.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Masons quoting stone fireplaces months ahead need to know where firebrick and veneer prices are heading. Built from invoices they share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Material costs swing; contributed data keeps it honest.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Campground and resort fire ring programs
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Resorts with stone fire rings and outdoor fireplaces sell evenings. A booking page for fireside sites and s'mores nights fills them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Hospitality owners spend on bookings and the mason built the features.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Sole fire feature mason per metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Fire features are a niche you can own in one metro. I build this for one mason per metro, and yours is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusivity in a small niche is a strong selling point.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue masonry sites hiding the fire work
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The mason with an outdated site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "If your site only talks about chimney repair, I can rebuild it around the fireplaces and pits people actually want."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The gap is obvious and the fire feature template is ready.
